contribution_after.assessment: The paper remains a useful synthesis rather than an independent major empirical breakthrough. Its core single-task ceiling comes from Davis et al. (2024) and its impossibility/heterogeneity intuition parallels Stroebl et al. (2024) and Chen et al. (2024), while the revision adds sound mean-preserving-spread bounds, fixes Proposition 4 and agreement generation accounting, and demonstrates empirically on 40 main and 25 harder items that self-verification fails disproportionately on repeated systematic errors and yields no reliable gain over single-attempt accuracy in the harder p = 0.58 regime. However, public-problem recall cues (34% main, 67% robust) continue to confound the stronger checker's measured accuracy.

summary: Revision round 1 closes 10 of 11 referee findings (F1-F2, F4-F11) and partially closes F3: theoretical claims, generation accounting, local-tool separation, scalable-oversight/automation-bias citations, caching sensitivity checks, and publication DOIs are repaired, and a 25-item robustness measurement plus explicit recall-cue quantification are added. F3 remains partially closed because the robustness set still uses public olympiad problems where recall cues rose (33/49 stronger-model checks) rather than uncontaminated items. Remaining minor issues are 2 visual label/line overlaps in Figure 1 (page 7), a stale Figure 2c caption (paper/PAPER.md:118) contradicting Section 5.2's generation-based agreement estimator, 1 slightly overcompressed abstract recall sentence (paper/PAPER.md:9), 1 paywalled source attribution (e-ridout) uncheckable at abstract depth, and unbound quantities in claims.yaml (4 clear omissions plus 4 unit/design counts).

verdicts.evidence: REVIEW/diff.patch:1929, 1944, 1977, 1986, 1991; paper/PAPER.md:9, 21, 58, 72, 76; simulation/output/results.json /theory_icc_counterexample. Abstract and Intro remove the false ICC monotonicity claim; Prop 2 adds 0<p<1, f>0, a<1, rho in (p,1); Prop 3(b) adds s>f>0; Section 4.2 states ICC does not fix the ceiling, presents the counterexample (0.706 at ICC=0.25 vs 0.738 at ICC=0.36), proves ordering by mean-preserving spread via Rothschild-Stiglitz (1970) and concavity, and scopes monotonicity to the Beta family in Figure 1c. All 14 tests in simulation/tests/test_theory.py and test_keys.py pass.
